originalTitle: Netanyahu rejects US-led 15-point Gaza peace plan in rare public break with Trump
summary: Israeli PM says IDF will not withdraw until Hamas is disarmed and rebukes US pressure to end wars without his country’s buy-in
content: Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has rejected a US-backed 15-point peace plan for Gaza in a rare public break with Donald Trump. In a statement on Sunday, Netanyahu said that he was confronting a “wave of rumours about Israeli weakness and Israeli withdrawals on all fronts” and rebuked US pressure to end wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran without Israel’s buy-in. On Gaza, he said: “Israel does not accept the 15-point document. The IDF will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is disarmed. And when I say the disarming of Hamas, it means heavy weaponry, lighter weaponry, all weaponry. And we are talking about genuine disarmament, not fictitious disarmament. Right now, we are talking with the Americans about this issue.” Trump’s Board of Peace in July proposed the 15-point plan, which mandated that Hamas disarm in exchange for providing a full Israeli military withdrawal from the Gaza Strip and an eventual transition of power to an independent Palestinian National Committee. Trump had said that the agreement would be implemented in stages, but Netanyahu on Sunday said that he wanted a full disarmament first in order to implement the deal. The Israeli leader’s main target in his remarks was the US. Israel has emerged as a key stumbling block in the Trump White House’s plans to broker peace in the region, in Israel’s conflicts in Gaza and Lebanon as well as in the war begun by joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran. And Netanyahu, who is facing tough elections in October and pressure from hardliners in his own government, appears ready to test his relationship with Trump in public in order to shore up his reputation as a defender of Israel at home. Israel had already signalled that it would reject the US-led plan. Soon after Trump announced it last month, Israel stepped up its bombing campaign in the Palestinian territory – strikes killed 18 people last Sunday. Netanyahu’s office had previously indicated it would not back the plan, saying: “The version that has been made public does not reflect Israel’s positions.” But Sunday’s rejection was far more forceful and direct, and appeared targeted at the Trump White House, as Trump and Netanyahu both face difficult elections. “Unlike all those who lecture us, we do what needs to be done for Israel’s security, and we can and know how to stand our ground, even against our best friends when necessary,” Netanyahu said. The head of Trump’s Board of Peace hit back on Sunday, saying the plan remained the “only way forward”. Nickolay Mladenov, the board’s high representative for Gaza, told Israeli television: “The option we are offering today is the only way forward that ensures this tragedy does not happen again.” Netanyahu’s rejection is a blow to Trump’s desire to be seen as a broker of peace in foreign conflicts. With US midterm elections due in November, the White House is desperate to negotiate a peace in Iran in order to reopen the strait of Hormuz and help bring down oil and petrol prices. But the conflicts in the Middle East are interconnected and parallel US efforts have continued to bring peace to Lebanon, where Israel has occupied land in what it says is a buffer zone against Hezbollah, and Gaza, where Gulf allies of the US have decried what they say is an ethnic cleansing campaign being carried out by Israel. Like US presidents before him, Trump has found that Netanyahu can be a difficult ally. Bill Clinton, after meeting Netanyahu for the first time in 1996, is reported to have said: “Who’s the fucking superpower here?” More recently, the Biden administration found that its concerns about the human toll in Gaza were ignored, but continued to publicly back Netanyahu and did not significantly suspend military aid to the country for fear of the political blowback that Netanyahu and his allies in the US could cause. In Trump, however, Netanyahu has found a far more unorthodox and unpredictable counterpart in the White House. Netanyahu is a natural ally for Trump, and he has attacked Democrats before the midterm elections for being weak on supporting Israel. Yet more broadly, support for Israel and its war in Gaza is eroding in the Democratic party, and the Republicans have a presidential frontrunner for 2028 in the vice-president, JD Vance, who is publicly sceptical of Israel and the war in Gaza. Trump will have to decide whether to increase pressure on Netanyahu, potentially alienating some pro-Israel allies, or to allow his efforts for a Gaza peace plan to stall, perhaps indefinitely. The answer will depend heavily on the US president’s own political instincts – are US voters hoping to see Trump emerge as a statesman capable of ending one of the world’s bloodiest recent wars in Gaza, or would a public clash with Netanyahu provoke a revolt among his base? With both countries entering tumultuous election cycles and a generational shift in support for Israel among US voters, the result could redraw the alliance between Israel and the US.
chineseTitle: 内塔尼亚胡拒绝美国主导的15点加沙和平计划，罕见地公开与特朗普决裂
chineseSummary: 以色列总理表示，在哈马斯解除武装之前，以色列国防军不会撤军，并斥责美国在没有以色列支持的情况下结束战争的压力
chineseContent: 以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡罕见地公开与唐纳德·特朗普决裂，拒绝了美国支持的加沙 15 点和平计划。内塔尼亚胡在周日的一份声明中表示，他面临着“关于以色列软弱和以色列在各方面撤军的谣言”，并斥责美国在没有以色列支持的情况下要求结束加沙、黎巴嫩和伊朗战争的压力。关于加沙，他说：“以色列不接受15点文件。在哈马斯解除武装之前，以色列国防军不会进行任何撤军。当我说哈马斯解除武装时，这意味着重型武器、轻型武器、所有武器。我们谈论的是真正的裁军，而不是虚假的裁军。现在，我们正在与美国人讨论这个问题。”特朗普的和平委员会7月提出了15点计划，要求哈马斯解除武装，以换取以色列从加沙地带全面撤军，并最终将权力移交给独立的巴勒斯坦全国委员会。特朗普曾表示该协议将分阶段实施，但内塔尼亚胡周日表示，他希望首先实现全面裁军，才能实施该协议。以色列领导人讲话的主要目标是美国。以色列已成为特朗普白宫斡旋该地区和平计划、以色列在加沙和黎巴嫩的冲突以及美以联合打击伊朗引发的战争的关键绊脚石。内塔尼亚胡正面临十月份的艰难选举和政府强硬派的压力，他似乎准备公开测试他与特朗普的关系，以巩固他作为以色列捍卫者在国内的声誉。以色列已经表示将拒绝美国主导的计划。特朗普上个月宣布这一消息后不久，以色列草原
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
